title: Elect sins not remitted from eternity—only in time when contracted guilt is actually loosed
source_text: XV. Porro ex iis quae dicta sunt patet, Electis ab aeterno peccata remissa non esse, sed illis demum in tempore remitti. Contrarium quidem afferunt Theologi nonnulli: sed perperam confundunt Dei decretum cum ejus executione. Nam Deus ab aeterno quidem decrevit electis peccata remittere, sed in tempore tantum peccata illis actu remittuntur. Quid enim est peccata remitti, nisi actu solvi reatum mortis aeternae, qui peccatis ante contractus est? Jam autem reatum illum electi solum in tempore contrahunt: dum, scilicet, peccato originali infecti nascuntur, & postquam adoleverunt in varia peccata incidunt: adeoque reatu illo possunt actu solum in tempore solvi.
pass_a_gloss: Further, from what has been said it is clear that sins have not been remitted to the elect from eternity, but are remitted to them only at last in time. Some theologians indeed assert the contrary; but they wrongly confuse God’s decree with its execution. For God from eternity indeed decreed to remit sins to the elect, but only in time are those sins actually remitted to them. For what is it for sins to be remitted, except that the guilt of eternal death previously contracted by sins be actually loosed? But the elect contract that guilt only in time: namely while they are born infected with original sin, and after they have grown up fall into various sins; and therefore they can be actually loosed from that guilt only in time.
pass_b_english: Decree ≠ execution: elect pardon is not eternal-actual but temporal-actual.
Guilt is contracted in time (original + actual); only then can it be actually loosed.
